title: FQXi: Reconciling Consciousness with Physicalism
description: Joscha Bach gives an introduction to the current debates about consciousness by going through the different metaphysical paradigms that people entertain. He then shows a computationalist perspective on the matter and dives into the structure of consciousness.

title: 32C3: Computational Metapsychology
description: “Minds cannot know truth, but they can generate meaning.” Bach dives into our epistemology and looks at certain structures in the brain to estimate and explain some of the inner workings of our mind.

title: 33C3: Machine Dreams
description: The TV series Westworld depicts a theme park in which humanoid robots are built by a perverse engineer-scientist to satisfy the desires of the theme park audience. We humans are built by a perverse evolution that needed a control system for social primates. In this talk, Bach addresses the notion of computation itself and elaborates on his conductor theory of consciousness.

title: 35C3: The Ghost in the Machine
description: Starting out with mathematics, computational mathematics, models, and functions, Bach arrives at the notions of purpose, free will, and consciousness.

title: 37C3: Synthetic Sentience
description: Joscha Bach gives a rationalist interpretation of Genesis I, addresses the phenomenal and functional notions of consciousness, and arrives at the notion of Cyber-Animism by looking at Japanese Animism through the lens of computationalist metaphysics.

title: 38C3: Self Models of Loving Grace
description: What am I? - Who is the self?

title: De Anima by Aristotle (4th century BCE)
description: Aristotle's foundational treatise on the psyche explores how perception, memory, and imagination work together, and characterizes its agency as an essential aspect of life and thought.

title: Meditations on First Philosophy by René Descartes (1641)
description: Descartes introduces the famous "I think, therefore I am," positioning consciousness as the core of self-certainty and exploring the duality between mind and body.

title: New Essays on Human Understanding by Gottfried Wilhem Leibniz (1704)
description: This text is Leibniz’s response to John Locke’s Essay Concerning Human Understanding. Leibniz argues that consciousness and knowledge are not entirely derived from experience,as Locke proposed, but also involve innate ideas. He explores the gradation of consciousness, from unconscious perceptions to clear self-awareness, and introduces his famous distinction between perception and apperception (conscious reflection).

title: L'Homme Machine by Julien Offray de La Mettrie (1748)
description: La Mettrie rejects dualist and idealist theories of the mind, and instead proposes a materialistic view, which sees humans as complex machines whose thoughts and feelings arise solely from physical processes.

title: The Critique of Pure Reason by Immanuel Kant (1781)
description: Kant examines how the mind structures experience, exploring how time, space, and causality shape our perception: a classical work that marks Kant's legacy as a cognitive scientist.

title: The Principles of Psychology by William James (1890)
description: James introduces the concept of the "stream of consciousness," analyzing how thoughts and perceptions form a continuous flow, integral to understanding self-awareness.

title: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus by Ludwig Wittgenstein (1921)
description: Wittgenstein's attempt to unify mathematics and thought was a major influence on Alan Turing.

title: A radical theory on consciousness
description: Joscha Bach gives a phenomenal and functional account of consciousness and then looks at the differences between self-organizing brains and current AI paradigms.

title: The podcast of this institute
Machine Learning Street Talk: Why your thoughts aren't yours
The Doors of Perception by Aldous Huxley (1954)
description: Huxley reflects on altered states of consciousness through psychedelic experiences, challenging conventional perceptions and exploring the potential expansiveness of the mind.

title: The Conscious Mind: In Search of a Fundamental Theory by David Chalmers (1996)
description: Chalmers highlights the difficulty of explaining consciousness through physical processes, presenting the "hard problem" of how subjective experience arises from the brain.

title: Permutation City by Greg Egan (1994)
description: Egan explores digital consciousness and mind uploading, presenting thought experiments about the continuity of self and simulated life in virtual worlds.

title: Closer (1992) and Diaspora (1997) by Greg Egan
description: Egan plays with identity and the creation and deconstruction of selfs, crossing over between human and artificial minds.

title: On the Life Cycle of Software Objects (2010) and Exhalation (2019) by Ted Chiang
description: Chiang presents AI beings with evolving personalities, and an intelligent entity exploring its own hardware and mind.

title: Blindsight (2006) and Echopraxia (2014) by Peter Watts
description: Probably the best collection of deliciously crafted possible minds, in lethal encounters between humanity, post human minds and alien intelligences.

title: He Who Shapes by Roger Zelazny (1965)
description: In this short story, Zelazny explores consciousness through a therapist’s mind-manipulation techniques and discovers the concept of the embedding space as the basis of mental representations. (Many of his books play with this concept in some form or other.)

title: Solaris by Stanislav Lem (1961)
description: The Polish novelist Lem is probably the most significant author of the cybernetic age. In the course of his thinking, he became increasingly pessimistic about the generality of intelligence. In "Solaris", he describes an encounter between humanity and a planet sized intelligence, and the fundamental incomprehensibility of minds far outside of the range of human capabilities.

title: Levels of Lucidity
description: An exploration of different levels of lucidity, focusing on how our perception interacts with awareness in various states of consciousness.

title: Bing - i observe
description: A song capturing the essence of observation and introspection, expressing the relationship between experience and awareness.

title: The Operation of Consciousness - AGI Conference
Existential Hope Salon: Joscha Bach x Lou de K
description: Past technological revolutions have led to human progress and increased well-being, but also to disruption, fear and existential dread. The AI revolution moves with a speed and potential for change that seems unprecedented. Will AI obliterate human agency? Tear down the economic, ecological, social and cultural foundations of our societies? Will it wipe out life on Earth to replace it with a dead machine world?

title: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis
description: This essay describes our philosophical position on machine consciousness, including what we mean by “machine” and “consciousness,” and the epistemological and metaphysical assumptions we make in approaching the question. It should be understood as a high-level overview of our core position and the ideas that inform it. We’re also working on a series of papers that address several of those ideas in greater depth and resolution.

title: Machine Consciousness
description: Cognitive scientist and AI researcher Joscha Bach explores artificial intelligence and consciousness. Bach elaborates on the history and philosophical underpinnings of AI, tracing its roots from Aristotle to contemporary deep learning. He discusses the current challenges and limitations in machine learning, particularly in achieving human-like understanding and consciousness.

title: Machine Consciousness & AI Awakening - Davidad and Joscha Bach
description:
Are today's AI systems conscious? What would it mean if they were? And what kind of future should we build if machine consciousness is possible?This first episode of our podcast series focuses on Machine Consciousness and the concept of an AI Awakening.

In this wide-ranging conversation, Joscha Bach (California Institute for Machine Consciousness) and Davidad explore some of the deepest questions at the intersection of AI, philosophy, cognitive science, and the future of civilization. Moderated by Lou de K (CIMC), the discussion was originally recorded ahead of the MC0001 conference (www.machine-consciousness.ai).

title: The Machine Consciousness Hypothesis - Joscha Bach, Hikari Sorensen and Lou de K
description:
